purpose: Headline findings from replacing self-generated corpus truth with an independent Gmsh -> CalculiX reference chain. These three statements are to survive into the write-up verbatim; the supporting numbers next to each are the evidence that backs them.
pipeline: Gmsh 4.13.1 (CAD-conforming tet10 from the case STEP file, order 2, HighOrderOptimize=2) -> CalculiX 2.23 ccx_static (C3D10, PaStiX direct sparse, OMP_NUM_THREADS=1) -> probe. Neither the PolyMesh mesher nor the PolyMesh solver takes part in any reference value.

findings.statement: The corpus "analytic" 3.0 is the infinite-plate idealisation and is 4-7% low for parts at d/W = 0.171-0.196, where the citable finite-width value is Howland 1930 via Roark ch.6 / Peterson chart 4.1 (Ktg 3.091-3.127) - our reference passed its own tol=0.1 by luck.

evidence.formula: Ktn = 3.000 - 3.140(d/W) + 3.667(d/W)^2 - 1.527(d/W)^3, sigma_nom = P/[t(W-d)]; on the gross-section stress the corpus probe uses, Ktg = Ktn/(1 - d/W)
evidence.citation: Howland, R.C.J. (1930) 'On the stresses in the neighbourhood of a circular hole in a strip under tension', Phil. Trans. R. Soc. London A 229:49-86; tabulated in Roark's Formulas for Stress and Strain ch.6 (central single circular hole in a finite-width plate, axial tension) and Peterson's Stress Concentration Factors chart 4.1
evidence.note: The residual +1.8% to +2.5% of the converged 3D CalculiX solve over the 2D handbook value is the finite-thickness effect (t/a of order 1) and is systematic in sign across all four regimes, which is the signature of correct 3D physics rather than pipeline error.
evidence.action_taken: All four box_hole *_c0 references now carry Ktg with the citation and the formula in metric.provenance.closed_form, and tol derived to cover the measured 3D gap.

findings.statement: CalculiX and our solver on one identical Gmsh mesh agree to 3.4e-9 in deflection and 6.7e-10 in strain energy, with our CLI independently reproducing the load area to 9 digits.

evidence.mesh: one identical Gmsh tet10 mesh: 5,250 nodes, 2,538 C3D10/tet10 elements, 15,387 DOF
evidence.polymesh_cli_log: load: 46 faces, area=7.55695102e-05 m2, total force -> |F|=75.5695102 N along (1 0 0) | Sf=(75.5695102 0 0) N, conservation err=1.42e-14 N
evidence.note: This extends the earlier hex8 result to tet10 on real corpus geometry: the solver is not the variable, the mesher is. It also means CalculiX-defined truth is directly comparable with our solver's output.

findings.statement: The Timoshenko bias is +1.0% to +2.4%, same sign everywhere, with deflection and energy self-consistent to 0.1% via U = P*delta/2 - the signature of a correct 3D solve against a stiffer beam idealisation, not of a pipeline error.

evidence.closed_form: Timoshenko stepped cantilever with Cowper shear correction, as documented in docs/validation/hand-calcs.md#corpus-primitives-cantilever
evidence.action_taken: These four references keep the closed form as their value (credibility ladder rank 1); the measured 3D gap is recorded in metric.provenance.external_confirmation and is carried in the derived tol.

supporting_verification.reproducibility: re-running a case after refactoring the load-face selection reproduced 3.207003104630254 (box_hole_s0_c0, normal_min_dot 0.7) and 7.8895245833704e-06 (stepped_shaft_s0_c1, normal_min_dot -1) bit-for-bit
supporting_verification.tet10_node_order: Gmsh msh type 11 -> Abaqus/CalculiX C3D10 permutation (0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7,9,8), verified against Gmsh's own -format inp exporter on 714/714 elements

mesh_sizing_policy_sensitivity.measured_on: box_hole_s0_c0 under two independent sizing policies (curvature 58 with MeshSizeMin h/12 at 86,481 DOF vs curvature 34 with MeshSizeMin h/5 at 64,614 DOF)
mesh_sizing_policy_sensitivity.note: global quantities are 370x less sensitive to the sizing policy than a nodal peak stress, which is why stress references carry larger derived tolerances

corrections_delivered.interpretation: The old values were produced by our own Cartesian grid-fill mesher, which we had already proven loses geometry silently. The largest corrections land exactly on the families where geometry loss was demonstrated (stepped_shaft up to +88%, sphere_box up to +65%), so the advisor was previously being scored against values that were wrong by up to a factor of 1.9.
